newsitem.title: FRANCE: Shorter hours at French battle tank firm save jobs.
newsitem.headline: Shorter hours at French battle tank firm save jobs.

text.p: Bosses and unions at French state arms maker Giat Industries have struck a deal to shorten working hours and save more than 900 jobs, unions said on Wednesday.
The deal hammered out late on Tuesday night after prolonged negotiations allows 932 planned redundancies to be cancelled out of a plan to shed 2,569 of Giat's 12,000 jobs in France.
France's largest union, the CFDT, said the accord would allow staff to cut their weekly working time to 35 hours and six minutes while being paid 98 percent compensation for the cut.
The statutory working week in France is 39 hours.
Workers can opt for an even shorter week of just over 31 hours in exchange for lower compensation, the CFDT said.
Giat makes the prestigious Leclerc battle tank which France hopes to sell to Saudi Arabia. But it has been forced by heavy losses into a reorganisation that enraged many of its staff.
Workers protesting about job cuts held 11 Giat executives hostage in October at a plant in southwest France.
Giat lost 10 billion francs ($1.9 billion) in 1995 and expects to make a further loss of 1.3 billion francs in 1996. ($ = 5.225 French Francs)
